subject: Civil Engineering
title: Truss Bridges: Triangles Across Rivers
description: A quick, practical guide to Truss Bridges: Triangles Across Rivers.

hook.text: Railroad bridges needed to span farther and carry heavier loads. Trusses answered.

buildup.text: Trusses use triangular patterns so every member carries pure tension or compression.

discovery.text: Different truss types — Pratt, Howe, Warren — optimize for different load patterns.

twist.text: Trusses are deep but lightweight — more material at top and bottom where stress peaks.

climax.text: The Quebec Bridge spans 1,800 feet using a cantilever truss — the longest of its type.

punchline.text: Triangles made railways cross rivers the world over.

quiz.question: Why are all truss members in either pure tension or compression?
options: Special bolts at the joints prevent any bending
The triangular geometry ensures forces only pull or push each bar axially
Truss members are made from a material that cannot bend
